name: Rule the candidate-facing register
text_content:
Type: founder decision

Canon governs every word the house writes and names no surface a candidate reads: its register matrix names six surfaces, none of them a recruiting or employee-facing one, "you" is specified for customer-facing contexts, and the Korean terminology rule does not say whether a document handed to a candidate is a brand context (finding 15.5). The team read one and could only mark it held: a posting is longer-form digital, candidate correspondence is correspondence, the seat sheet on the team home is in-space copy's cousin, "you" is correct to a candidate, and the Korean terms stay out of postings and are taught inside the house rather than glossed to a stranger (P22). This is a brand fact and the team does not assert it; canon's owner closes it, alongside canon's own deferred terminology session. Readiness row 39 runs on the team's reading while held and is re-run when the ruling lands. Does not block a hire; blocks a posting going live as written.

Filed by Session 5 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmhm4. Reasoning lives on the S5 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

Session 12 also files that canon's Nunchi, "not diagnostic inquiry," sits against coaching by hypothesis (finding 18.4), with the team's reading that a hypothesis is about an act at a table and never about a person's Nunchi. S12 page, section 13; P38 to P40.

comment.text: Session 11 adds the employee-facing register as the same ruling. The team reads a house-written internal page as correspondence's cousin with "we" as the house and "you" to the person, every sentence under the six binary tests; the brief as speech reading a record's words; the check-in as a conversation canon does not script; and a person's own words as carrying the language constant only. Whether an internal page is a brand context, which decides whether canon's Korean terms may be said to ask something of a seat without being defined, is the same question Session 5 asked for a candidate's document and Session 7 for a module. One ruling closes all three. S11 page, sections 8.4 and 9; P19, P23, P24; instrument I4.
